doc.title: Joseph Rene and Edna Kelly Interview, 1969-12-15

title: Chris's favorite musicians and the music he liked
summary: Edna says Chris favoured slow, soft music and lists old songs he played, and that he was liked by everyone.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Chris Kelly, the blues trumpeter and his band

blocks.x: Okay. Did, what did, did Chris ever say who he liked or what his favorite, who his favorite musicians were or say anybody he liked to play?
That's who I'm talking about right now. George, Will Humphrey, and Faisal, and Lil' Kit Howard, the one that I was telling about. And that's Chris Howard, isn't he? No.
And did he ever say anything about how he liked to play music or how he thought music ought to be played?
Oh, he loved it. He could just spit music out, it looked like. He just loved it. Played it for a natural living.

And did he have any, did he ever, did he, did he ever say anything to you about how he, he, he liked it to be? You know, how he liked, what kind of music did he like? Jazz. What, what kind of music did he like? Do you remember? Did he say? Jazz player. Jazz player. But did he say he liked slow music or fast music or fast music or?

Slow music. Slow music, you know, like night, like night club. Like night club, you know, soft music. Because he used to put a music in his home and he played music. stuff Oh, I know so many numbers now. I do. When my dreamboat come home, old song, yeah. Meet me tonight in the moonlight. Old time song. That's before you were born. Yes, I don't remember that one.
Do you remember any more? Good Night, Irene.
His specialty was that carousel, right?
Did the people want him to play that?
They loved it. Did he play a long number? Did he play it for a long time?
And then another piece he's placed by the name of Stumbling All Around. Oh, yes.
They play. They must all the mutants come around. It's been a long time.
And he was a popular man. Everybody liked him. He was a well-liked man.
